newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 23.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Cabinet 'palace' suffers setback: The Cabinet suffered a setback on Thursday whan a parliamentary select committee called for public submissions on the proposed NZ$94 million building for Cabinet ministers, criticised as "lavish" by Opposition MPs. Page 1.

Spy committee set up despite niggling: Parliament has finally established its intelligence and security committee after another argument on Thursday about its functions and the method used to appoint members. Page 2.
Bill for super referendum passes: Legislation paving the way for September's referendum on compulsory superannuation passed its final stages in Parliament after a two-hour debate on Thursday. Page 2.

Peters invites Moore and Burdon: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters will be accompanied by former overseas trade ministers Philip Burdon and Mike Moore when he represents New Zealand at the official handover of Hong Kong to China next month. Page 2.
Luxton calls for more privatisation: More than 80 percent of government activity could be done by the private sector, Commerce Minister John Luxton said on Thursday. Page 13.
Pay rates rise 2.2 percent in quarter: Overall wage and salary increases for the March quarter were the highest in six years, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday. Page 13.
Powerco makes $18m profit: Taranaki-Wanganui power company Powerco on Thursday reported an $18 million after-tax profit for the year to March, the company's first full year of operation. Page 13.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Drink-related road deaths cut in half: Alcohol-related deaths on New Zealand roads have dropped by 50 percent over the past seven years, but the government and the police are not relenting in the fight against drink-drivers.
Keen contest for TV net sale: Several television companies are indicating interest in the last set of nationwide television licenses which go up for sale this weekend.
Closed PC Mag may get reboot: An Australian publishing company is considering relaunching the recently-closed PC Magazine in New Zealand.
Mercury sees cost cuts: Mercury Energy's cost of electricity is expected to drop when it fires up its Poihipi geothermal power plant in around three weeks.

Collapse of Bre-X affects NZ Petroleum: The flow-on effects of the collapse of Canadian-based gold explorer Bre-X mean New Zealand Petroleum is likely to record a loss in its financial year ending May 31.

Paynter change: Paynter Timber Ltd's sale of native South Westland forest to the government was part of a turnaround in the company's stance on native logging, executive director Don MacLachlan said on Thursday.
Boom seen for plastics industry: A huge increase in the consumption of plastics in Asia is expected to lead to a boom in exports and long-wanted growth for the New Zealand plastics industry.
THE PRESS
Port stake pointless -- Shadwell: The Christchurch City Council is speculating with its 65.6 percent stake in the Lyttelton Port Company, says Alan Shadwell, a former port chairman. Page 18.
'Reasonable' profit for INL, says Robson: Independent Newspapers Ltd's profit will be "reasonable" in its latest June 30 year, the managing director, Mike Robson, says. Page 18.
Markets unworried over wages lift: Higher wages and salaries data, boosted by teachers' earnings, do not have immediate implications for financial markets, analysts say. Page 18.
New offering of Telenotes: Terms for a new Telenote offering were announced on Thursday by Telecom's TCNZ Finance. Page 18.
